llm.summary: This is a local Chinese countdown/anniversary helper that stores user-entered dates in one disclosed local JSON file and does not show network, credential, or hidden execution behavior.

dimensions.detail: Local read/write access is proportionate to the stated purpose and appears limited to ~/.qclaw/workspace/countdown.json; no broad filesystem indexing, credential access, subprocess execution, or network calls were found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No formal permission manifest was present beyond the skill metadata, but the artifact documents the exact local storage path and the script has no package install or remote retrieval steps.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited to explicit CLI commands for managing countdown entries; there are no role-changing instructions, prompt overrides, or hidden agent-control behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence consists of user-directed countdown records saved locally in a JSON file. There are no services, scheduled tasks, shell profile edits, memory writes, or privilege escalation behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core behavior matches a countdown/date utility: add, edit, delete, list, and calculate dates. The claimed lunar support appears underimplemented in the script, but this is a quality issue rather than a security concern.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, expect a local CLI tool that saves event names, dates, tags, and notes in ~/.qclaw/workspace/countdown.json. Avoid storing highly sensitive personal details there, and treat the external website links at the end of the documentation as publisher promotion rather than part of the countdown feature.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The script reads and writes a local JSON data file, which is expected for a local countdown manager; the storage path is disclosed in SKILL.md and code review found no broader file access.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only naming, documentation, and CLI text are consistent with a Chinese-language countdown tool and do not create a security concern, though users needing other locales should know this limitation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The homepage and promotional diagnosis links are unrelated to countdown functionality, but they are visible documentation links only; no automatic network access or redirection behavior was found.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The promotional call-to-action is not needed for the tool's operation, but it is disclosed in the skill text and does not materially change runtime authority.
[SQP-3] expected: The script help text is Chinese-only, matching the advertised audience and not indicating hidden or unsafe behavior.
